claims.text: Sustained loading at intermediate temperatures progressively activates plastic deformation in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers.
Local lattice distortions and short-range chemical clustering at coherent FCC/BCC interfaces reduce the barrier for dislocation climb.
Reduced climb barriers enable gradual transfer of dislocations from softer FCC layers into stronger BCC layers.
The starting multilayer has coherent or semi-coherent FCC/BCC interfaces, low defect densities, and chemical short-range order.
At an intermediate temperature, sustained constant stress can activate dislocation climb without causing full recrystallization.
Applying stresses below the immediate-flow yield point will preserve the nanoscale multilayer microstructure while allowing progressive plasticity to be measured.
Coherent FCC/BCC interfaces act as the structural mediator of dislocation activation and transfer.
Dislocations initially nucleate in the relatively softer FCC layers.
Dislocations accumulate at FCC/BCC interfaces because of lattice mismatch and short-range ordering.
Stress-assisted dislocation climb can be an operative creep mechanism in a high-entropy alloy.
Lattice distortion and compositional clustering facilitate stress-assisted climb in the proposed multilayer.
Interface-mediated climb produces coordinated progressive plasticity without compromising the nanoscale multilayer architecture.
The creep strain rate will initially be low and then gradually accelerate as climb and interface activity become dominant.
Deformed specimens will exhibit interfacial dislocation pile-ups, jogs, and local rearrangements correlated with chemical clustering or ordering.
Jog configurations are indicative of dislocation climb.
The proposed mechanism should be suppressed at cryogenic temperatures and may be displaced by dynamic recrystallization or grain-boundary sliding at very high temperatures.
Annealing can be used to reduce interfacial short-range order while otherwise retaining an identical comparison specimen.
The as-deposited specimens should show more climb markers than annealed specimens with reduced interfacial short-range order.
Failure to observe the predicted comparative increase in climb markers or a correlation between plasticity and interfacial climb would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
